claim: A cornerstone of theoretical neuroscience is the circuit model: a system of equations that captures a hypothesized neural mechanism.
source: A cornerstone of theoretical neuroscience is the circuit model: a system of equations that captures a hypothesized neural mechanism.
evidence: This is a statement about the field of theoretical neuroscience that is presented as established knowledge.

claim: Circuit models are valuable when they give rise to an experimentally observed phenomenon.
source: Such models are valuable when they give rise to an experimentally observed phenomenon -- whether behavioral or a pattern of neural activity -- and thus can offer insights into neural computation.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of circuit models based on established understanding in the field.

claim: The operation of circuit models critically depends on the choice of model parameters.
source: The operation of these circuits, like all models, critically depends on the choice of model parameters.
evidence: This is a general statement about models that is presented as established knowledge.

claim: A key step in circuit modeling is to identify the model parameters consistent with observed phenomena: to solve the inverse problem.
source: A key step is then to identify the model parameters consistent with observed phenomena: to solve the inverse problem.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodology of circuit modeling presented as established practice.

claim: This work presents a novel technique called emergent property inference (EPI) that brings the modern probabilistic modeling toolkit to theoretical neuroscience.
source: In this work, we present a novel technique, emergent property inference (EPI), that brings the modern probabilistic modeling toolkit to theoretical neuroscience.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the contribution of the manuscript.

claim: Theoreticians predominantly focus on reproducing computational properties rather than a particular dataset when theorizing circuit models.
source: When theorizing circuit models, theoreticians predominantly focus on reproducing computational properties rather than a particular dataset.
evidence: This is a statement about the practice of theoreticians in the field.

claim: EPI uses deep neural networks to learn parameter distributions with computational properties.
source: Our method uses deep neural networks to learn parameter distributions with these computational properties.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the methodology of EPI.

claim: EPI is introduced through a motivational example of parameter inference in the stomatogastric ganglion.
source: This methodology is introduced through a motivational example of parameter inference in the stomatogastric ganglion.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure of the manuscript.

claim: EPI allows precise control over the behavior of inferred parameters.
source: EPI is then shown to allow precise control over the behavior of inferred parameters and to scale in parameter dimension better than alternative techniques.
evidence: This is a claim about the capabilities of EPI that is supported by results presented in the manuscript.

claim: EPI scales in parameter dimension better than alternative techniques.
source: EPI is then shown to allow precise control over the behavior of inferred parameters and to scale in parameter dimension better than alternative techniques.
evidence: This is a claim about the performance of EPI compared to other methods, supported by results in the manuscript.

claim: Novel theoretical findings in models of primary visual cortex and superior colliculus were gained through the examination of complex parametric structure captured by EPI.
source: In the remainder of this work, we present novel theoretical findings in models of primary visual cortex and superior colliculus, which were gained through the examination of complex parametric structure captured by EPI.
evidence: This is a statement about the scientific contributions of the manuscript.

claim: The fundamental practice of theoretical neuroscience is to use a mathematical model to understand neural computation.
source: The fundamental practice of theoretical neuroscience is to use a mathematical model to understand neural computation, whether that computation enables perception, action, or some intermediate processing.
evidence: This is a statement about the field of theoretical neuroscience presented as established knowledge.

claim: Neural circuits are systematized with a set of equations motivated by biophysics, neurophysiology, and other conceptual considerations.
source: A neural circuit is systematized with a set of equations – the model – and these equations are motivated by biophysics, neurophysiology, and other conceptual considerations (Kopell and Ermentrout, 1988; Marder, 1998; Abbott, 2008; Wang, 2010; O'Leary et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about the practice of modeling neural circuits, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The function of a neural circuit model is governed by the choice of model parameters.
source: The function of this system is governed by the choice of model parameters, which when configured in a particular way, give rise to a measurable signature of a computation.
evidence: This is a general statement about models presented as established knowledge.

claim: The inverse problem is crucial for reasoning about likely parameter values, uniquenesses and degeneracies, and predictions made by the model.
source: The inverse problem is crucial for reasoning about likely parameter values, uniquenesses and degeneracies, and predictions made by the model (Gutenkunst et al., 2007; Erguler and Stumpf, 2011; Mannakee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of the inverse problem, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Seminal examples of analytical derivation in theoretical neuroscience include understanding of memory capacity in associative neural networks.
source: Seminal examples of this gold standard include our field's understanding of memory capacity in associative neural networks (Hopfield, 1982), chaos and autocorrelation timescales in random neural networks (Sompolinsky et al., 1988), central pattern generation (Olypher and Calabrese, 2007), the paradoxical effect (Tsodyks et al., 1997), and decision making (Wong and Wang, 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about seminal work in the field, supported by citations.

claim: As circuit models include more biological realism, theory via analytical derivation becomes intractable.
source: Unfortunately, as circuit models include more biological realism, theory via analytical derivation becomes intractable.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of analytical methods in complex models, presented as established understanding.

claim: Statistical inference offers a toolkit to solve the inverse problem by identifying the distribution of parameters that produce computations in a biologically realistic model.
source: Absent this analysis, statistical inference offers a toolkit by which to solve the inverse problem by identifying, at least approximately, the distribution of parameters that produce computations in a biologically realistic model (Foster et al., 1993; Prinz et al., 2004; Achard and De Schutter, 2006; Fisher et al., 2013; O'Leary et al., 2014; Alonso and Marder, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the use of statistical inference in neuroscience, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In neuroscience, computation is often quantified using an exemplar dataset.
source: First, often we directly use an exemplar dataset: a collection of samples that express the computation of interest, this data being gathered either experimentally in the lab or from a computer simulation.
evidence: This is a statement about a common practice in neuroscience.

claim: Exemplar datasets are well known to have features irrelevant to the computation of interest.
source: Although a natural choice given its connection to experiment (Paninski and Cunningham, 2018), some drawbacks exist: these data are well known to have features irrelevant to the computation of interest (Niell and Stryker, 2010; Saleem et al., 2013; Musall et al., 2019), confounding inferences made on such data.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of using exemplar datasets, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Researchers often quantify an emergent property: a statistic of data that directly quantifies the computation of interest.
source: Alternatively, researchers often quantify an emergent property (EP): a statistic of data that directly quantifies the computation of interest, wherein the dataset is implicit.
evidence: This is a statement about an alternative approach to quantifying computation in neuroscience.

claim: The 'gold standard' examples in theoretical neuroscience all quantify and focus on some derived feature of the data, rather than the data drawn from the model.
source: While such a choice may seem esoteric, it is not: the above 'gold standard' examples (Hopfield, 1982; Sompolinsky et al., 1988; Olypher and Calabrese, 2007; Tsodyks et al., 1997; Wong and Wang, 2006) all quantify and focus on some derived feature of the data, rather than the data drawn from the model.
evidence: This is a statement about the approach taken in seminal work in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The statistical framework of emergent property inference is intimately connected to the literature on approximate bayesian computation.
source: This statistical framework is not new: it is intimately connected to the literature on approximate bayesian computation (Beaumont et al., 2002; Marjoram et al., 2003; Sisson et al., 2007), parameter sensitivity analyses (Raue et al., 2009; Karlsson et al., 2012; Hines et al., 2014; Raman et al., 2017), maximum entropy modeling (Elsayed and Cunningham, 2017; Savin and Tkačik, 2017; Młynarski et al., 2020), and approximate bayesian inference (Tran et al., 2017; Gonçalves et al., 2019); we detail these connections in Section 'Related approaches'.
evidence: This is a statement about the relationship of EPI to prior work, supported by citations.

claim: The parameter distributions producing a computation may be curved or multimodal along various parameter axes and combinations.
source: The parameter distributions producing a computation may be curved or multimodal along various parameter axes and combinations.
evidence: This is a statement about the complexity of parameter distributions, presented as established understanding.

claim: Traditional approximation families (e.g. mean-field or mixture of gaussians) are limited in the distributional structure they may learn.
source: Traditional approximation families (e.g. mean-field or mixture of gaussians) are limited in the distributional structure they may learn.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of traditional methods, presented as established knowledge.

claim: Advances in machine learning have used deep probability distributions as flexible approximating families for complicated distributions.
source: To address such restrictions on expressivity, advances in machine learning have used deep probability distributions as flexible approximating families for such complicated distributions (Rezende and Mohamed, 2015; Papamakarios et al., 2019a) (see Section 'Deep probability distributions and normalizing flows').
evidence: This is a statement about advances in machine learning, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The adaptation of deep probability distributions to the problem of theoretical circuit analysis requires recent developments in deep learning for constrained optimization.
source: However, the adaptation of deep probability distributions to the problem of theoretical circuit analysis requires recent developments in deep learning for constrained optimization (Loaiza-Ganem et al., 2017), and architectural choices for efficient and expressive deep generative modeling (Dinh et al., 2017; Kingma and Dhariwal, 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the technical requirements for EPI, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: EPI demonstrates its ability to handle biologically realistic circuit models using a five-neuron model of the stomatogastric ganglion.
source: First, we show EPI's ability to handle biologically realistic circuit models using a five-neuron model of the stomatogastric ganglion (Gutierrez et al., 2013): a neural circuit whose parametric degeneracy is closely studied (Goldman et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement about a demonstration of EPI in the manuscript, supported by citations to prior work on the STG model.

claim: EPI shows scalability to high dimensional parameter distributions by inferring connectivities of recurrent neural networks that exhibit stable, yet amplified responses.
source: Then, we show EPI's scalability to high dimensional parameter distributions by inferring connectivities of recurrent neural networks that exhibit stable, yet amplified responses – a hallmark of neural responses throughout the brain (Murphy and Miller, 2009; Hennequin et al., 2014; Bondanelli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about a demonstration of EPI in the manuscript, supported by citations to prior work on stable amplification.

claim: In a model of primary visual cortex, EPI reveals how the recurrent processing across different neuron-type populations shapes excitatory variability.
source: In a model of primary visual cortex (Litwin-Kumar et al., 2016; Palmigiano et al., 2020), EPI reveals how the recurrent processing across different neuron-type populations shapes excitatory variability: a finding that we show is analytically intractable.
evidence: This is a statement about a finding from applying EPI to a V1 model, supported by citations to prior work on the model.

claim: EPI investigated the possible connectivities of a superior colliculus model that allow execution of different tasks on interleaved trials.
source: Finally, we investigated the possible connectivities of a superior colliculus model that allow execution of different tasks on interleaved trials (Duan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about an application of EPI to an SC model, supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: EPI discovered a rich distribution containing two connectivity regimes with different solution classes in the superior colliculus model.
source: EPI discovered a rich distribution containing two connectivity regimes with different solution classes.
evidence: This is a statement about a finding from applying EPI to an SC model.

claim: The inferred connectivities of each regime in the SC model reproduced results from optogenetic inactivation experiments in markedly different ways.
source: Intriguingly, the inferred connectivities of each regime reproduced results from optogenetic inactivation experiments in markedly different ways.
evidence: This is a statement about a finding from applying EPI to an SC model.

claim: The stomatogastric ganglion (STG) of crustaceans is a small neural circuit which generates multiple rhythmic muscle activation patterns for digestion.
source: To ground this process in a well-known example, consider the stomatogastric ganglion (STG) of crustaceans, a small neural circuit which generates multiple rhythmic muscle activation patterns for digestion (Marder and Thirumalai, 2002).
evidence: This is a statement about the STG, supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Despite full knowledge of STG connectivity and a precise characterization of its rhythmic pattern generation, biophysical models of the STG have complicated relationships between circuit parameters and computation.
source: Despite full knowledge of STG connectivity and a precise characterization of its rhythmic pattern generation, biophysical models of the STG have complicated relationships between circuit parameters and computation (Goldman et al., 2001; Prinz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a statement about the complexity of STG models, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The fast population in the STG subcircuit model represents the subnetwork generating the pyloric rhythm.
source: The fast population (f1 and f2) represents the subnetwork generating the pyloric rhythm and the slow population (s1 and s2) represents the subnetwork of the gastric mill rhythm.
evidence: This is a statement about the STG model, supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The slow population in the STG subcircuit model represents the subnetwork of the gastric mill rhythm.
source: The fast population (f1 and f2) represents the subnetwork generating the pyloric rhythm and the slow population (s1 and s2) represents the subnetwork of the gastric mill rhythm.
evidence: This is a statement about the STG model, supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The two fast neurons in the STG subcircuit model mutually inhibit one another.
source: The two fast neurons mutually inhibit one another, and spike at a greater frequency than the mutually inhibiting slow neurons.
evidence: This is a statement about the STG model, supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The fast neurons in the STG subcircuit model spike at a greater frequency than the mutually inhibiting slow neurons.
source: The two fast neurons mutually inhibit one another, and spike at a greater frequency than the mutually inhibiting slow neurons.
evidence: This is a statement about the STG model, supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The hub neuron in the STG subcircuit model couples with either the fast or slow population, or both depending on modulatory conditions.
source: The hub neuron couples with either the fast or slow population, or both depending on modulatory conditions.
evidence: This is a statement about the STG model, supported by reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The emergent property of intermediate hub frequency is defined by the hub neuron firing at an intermediate frequency between the intrinsic spiking rates of the fast and slow populations.
source: An emergent property studied by Gutierrez et al. is the hub neuron firing at an intermediate frequency between the intrinsic spiking rates of the fast and slow populations.
evidence: This is a statement about the emergent property studied in the STG model, supported by reference to prior work.

claim: Intermediate hub frequency is defined not strictly as 0.55 Hz, but frequencies of moderate deviation from 0.55 Hz between the fast (.35Hz) and slow (.68Hz) frequencies.
source: To be precise, we define intermediate hub frequency not strictly as 0.55 Hz, but frequencies of moderate deviation from 0.55 Hz between the fast (.35Hz) and slow (.68Hz) frequencies.
evidence: This is a statement about how the emergent property is defined in the manuscript.

claim: EPI takes, as input, the model and the specified emergent property, and as its output, returns the parameter distribution.
source: EPI (Figure 1D) takes, as input, the model and the specified emergent property, and as its output, returns the parameter distribution (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a statement about the EPI method, supported by reference to Figure 1D and 1E.

claim: The EPI distribution is a parameter distribution constrained such that the circuit model produces the emergent property.
source: This distribution – represented for clarity as samples from the distribution – is a parameter distribution constrained such that the circuit model produces the emergent property.
evidence: This is a statement about the EPI distribution.

claim: Once EPI is run, the returned distribution can be used to efficiently generate additional parameter samples.
source: Once EPI is run, the returned distribution can be used to efficiently generate additional parameter samples.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of EPI.

claim: The inferred distribution from EPI can be efficiently queried to quantify the parametric structure that it captures.
source: Most importantly, the inferred distribution can be efficiently queried to quantify the parametric structure that it captures.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of EPI.

claim: EPI formalizes the three-step procedure of model selection, emergent property specification, and parameter inference with deep probability distributions.
source: EPI formalizes the three-step procedure of the previous section with deep probability distributions (Rezende and Mohamed, 2015; Papamakarios et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is a statement about the EPI method, supported by citations to prior work on deep probability distributions.

claim: In general, an emergent property is a collection of constraints on statistical moments that together define the computation of interest.
source: In general, an emergent property is a collection of constraints on statistical moments that together define the computation of interest.
evidence: This is a statement about the definition of emergent properties in EPI.

claim: Deep probability distributions are far more flexible and capable of fitting rich structure than simpler classes of distributions like the gaussian or mixture of gaussians.
source: In contrast to simpler classes of distributions like the gaussian or mixture of gaussians, deep probability distributions are far more flexible and capable of fitting rich structure (Rezende and Mohamed, 2015; Papamakarios et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is a statement about deep probability distributions, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Once optimized, the deep network representation of a distribution has remarkably useful properties: fast sampling and probability evaluations.
source: Once optimized, this deep network representation of a distribution has remarkably useful properties: fast sampling and probability evaluations.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of deep probability distributions.

claim: Fast probability evaluations confer fast gradient and Hessian calculations as well.
source: Importantly, fast probability evaluations confer fast gradient and Hessian calculations as well.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of deep probability distributions.

claim: Unlike alternative techniques, once an EPI distribution has been learned, the modes and Hessians of the distribution can be measured with trivial computation.
source: Importantly and unlike alternative techniques, once an EPI distribution has been learned, the modes and Hessians of the distribution can be measured with trivial computation (see Section 'Deep probability distributions and normalizing flows').
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of EPI compared to other methods.

claim: Transient amplification is a hallmark of neural activity throughout cortex and is often thought to be intrinsically generated by recurrent connectivity in the responding cortical area.
source: Transient amplification is a hallmark of neural activity throughout cortex and is often thought to be intrinsically generated by recurrent connectivity in the responding cortical area (Murphy and Miller, 2009; Hennequin et al., 2014; Bondanelli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about neural activity, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: To generate amplified, yet stabilized responses, the connectivity of RNNs must be non-normal.
source: It has been shown that to generate such amplified, yet stabilized responses, the connectivity of RNNs must be non-normal (Goldman, 2009; Murphy and Miller, 2009), and satisfy additional constraints (Bondanelli and Ostojic, 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about RNN connectivity, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In theoretical neuroscience, RNNs are optimized and then examined to show how dynamical systems could execute a given computation.
source: In theoretical neuroscience, RNNs are optimized and then examined to show how dynamical systems could execute a given computation (Sussillo, 2014; Barak, 2017), but such biologically realistic constraints on connectivity (Goldman, 2009; Murphy and Miller, 2009; Bondanelli and Ostojic, 2020) are ignored for simplicity or because constrained optimization is difficult.
evidence: This is a statement about the use of RNNs in theoretical neuroscience, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Access to distributions of connectivity that produce theoretical criteria like stable amplification, chaotic fluctuations, or low tangling would add scientific value to existing research with RNNs.
source: In general, access to distributions of connectivity that produce theoretical criteria like stable amplification, chaotic fluctuations (Sompolinsky et al., 1988), or low tangling (Russo et al., 2018) would add scientific value to existing research with RNNs.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential value of EPI for RNN research, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ABC techniques struggle in parameter spaces of modest dimension.
source: It is well known that ABC techniques struggle in parameter spaces of modest dimension (Sisson et al., 2018), yet we were careful to assess the scalability of SNPE, which is a more closely related methodology to EPI.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of ABC techniques, supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Deep inference techniques EPI and SNPE are far more amenable to inference of high dimensional RNN connectivities than rejection sampling techniques like SMC-ABC.
source: In this analysis, we see that deep inference techniques EPI and SNPE are far more amenable to inference of high dimensional RNN connectivities than rejection sampling techniques like SMC-ABC, and that EPI outperforms SNPE in both wall time (elapsed real time) and simulation count.
evidence: This is a statement about the performance of EPI and SNPE compared to SMC-ABC, supported by the analysis in the manuscript.

claim: EPI outperforms SNPE in both wall time and simulation count.
source: In this analysis, we see that deep inference techniques EPI and SNPE are far more amenable to inference of high dimensional RNN connectivities than rejection sampling techniques like SMC-ABC, and that EPI outperforms SNPE in both wall time (elapsed real time) and simulation count.
evidence: This is a statement about the performance of EPI compared to SNPE, supported by the analysis in the manuscript.

claim: When using SNPE, the predictions of the inferred parameters are highly concentrated at some RNN sizes and widely varied in others.
source: When using SNPE, the predictions of the inferred parameters are highly concentrated at some RNN sizes and widely varied in others (Figure 2C, orange).
evidence: This is a statement about the performance of SNPE, supported by reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The choice to use gradient information agrees with recent speculation that such gradient information could improve the efficiency of simulation-based inference techniques.
source: This choice agrees with recent speculation that such gradient information could improve the efficiency of simulation-based inference techniques (Cranmer et al., 2020), as well as reflecting the classic tradeoff between gradient-based and sampling-based estimators (scaling and speed versus generality).
evidence: This is a statement about the relationship of EPI to prior work, supported by a citation.

claim: If the emergent property gradient is efficiently calculated, EPI is a clear choice for inferring high dimensional parameter distributions.
source: Since gradients of the emergent property are necessary in EPI optimization, gradient tractability is a key criteria when determining the suitability of a simulation-based inference technique. If the emergent property gradient is efficiently calculated, EPI is a clear choice for inferring high dimensional parameter distributions.
evidence: This is a statement about when EPI is a good choice.

claim: Dynamical models of excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) populations with supralinear input-output function have succeeded in explaining a host of experimentally documented phenomena in primary visual cortex (V1).
source: Dynamical models of excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) populations with supralinear input-output function have succeeded in explaining a host of experimentally documented phenomena in primary visual cortex (V1).
evidence: This is a statement about the success of E-I models in explaining V1 phenomena.

claim: In a regime characterized by inhibitory stabilization of strong recurrent excitation, E-I models give rise to paradoxical responses, selective amplification, surround suppression, and normalization.
source: In a regime characterized by inhibitory stabilization of strong recurrent excitation, these models give rise to paradoxical responses (Tsodyks et al., 1997), selective amplification (Goldman, 2009; Murphy and Miller, 2009), surround suppression (Ozeki et al., 2009), and normalization (Rubin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about the phenomena that E-I models can produce, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Recent theoretical work shows that stabilized E-I models reproduce the effect of variability suppression.
source: Recent theoretical work (Hennequin et al., 2018) shows that stabilized E-I models reproduce the effect of variability suppression (Churchland et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about recent theoretical work, supported by citations.

claim: Experimental evidence shows that inhibition is composed of distinct elements – parvalbumin (P), somatostatin (S), VIP (V) – composing 80% of GABAergic interneurons in V1.
source: Furthermore, experimental evidence shows that inhibition is composed of distinct elements – parvalbumin (P), somatostatin (S), VIP (V) – composing 80% of GABAergic interneurons in V1 (Markram et al., 2004; Rudy et al., 2011; Tremblay et al., 2016), and that these inhibitory cell types follow specific connectivity patterns (Figure 3A; Pfeffer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental evidence, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Inhibitory cell types in V1 follow specific connectivity patterns.
source: Furthermore, experimental evidence shows that inhibition is composed of distinct elements – parvalbumin (P), somatostatin (S), VIP (V) – composing 80% of GABAergic interneurons in V1 (Markram et al., 2004; Rudy et al., 2011; Tremblay et al., 2016), and that these inhibitory cell types follow specific connectivity patterns (Figure 3A; Pfeffer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental evidence, supported by citations to prior work and reference to Figure 3A.

claim: EPI is used on a model of V1 with biologically realistic connectivity to show how the structure of input across neuron types affects the variability of the excitatory population.
source: Here, we use EPI on a model of V1 with biologically realistic connectivity to show how the structure of input across neuron types affects the variability of the excitatory population – the population largely responsible for projecting to other brain areas (Felleman and Van Essen, 1991).
evidence: This is a statement about the application of EPI to a V1 model, supported by a citation.

claim: The excitatory population is largely responsible for projecting to other brain areas.
source: Here, we use EPI on a model of V1 with biologically realistic connectivity to show how the structure of input across neuron types affects the variability of the excitatory population – the population largely responsible for projecting to other brain areas (Felleman and Van Essen, 1991).
evidence: This is a statement about the role of the excitatory population, supported by a citation.

claim: Stochasticity and inhibitory multiplicity introduce substantial complexity to the mathematical treatment of the V1 model.
source: Stochasticity and inhibitory multiplicity introduce substantial complexity to the mathematical treatment of this problem (see Section 'Primary visual cortex: Mathematical intuition and challenges') motivating the analysis of this model with EPI.
evidence: This is a statement about the complexity of the V1 model, with reference to a later section.

claim: The strong interaction between E- and P-population input variability on excitatory variability is intriguing, since this circuit exhibits a paradoxical effect in the P-population.
source: The strong interaction between E- and P-population input variability on excitatory variability is intriguing, since this circuit exhibits a paradoxical effect in the P-population (and no other inhibitory types) (Figure 3—figure supplement 4), meaning that the E-population is P-stabilized.
evidence: This is a statement about the interpretation of the results, supported by reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The E-population is P-stabilized.
source: The strong interaction between E- and P-population input variability on excitatory variability is intriguing, since this circuit exhibits a paradoxical effect in the P-population (and no other inhibitory types) (Figure 3—figure supplement 4), meaning that the E-population is P-stabilized.
evidence: This is a statement about the V1 model, supported by reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Future research may uncover a link between the population of network stabilization and compensatory interactions governing excitatory variability.
source: Future research may uncover a link between the population of network stabilization and compensatory interactions governing excitatory variability.
evidence: This is a statement about potential future research.

claim: EPI revealed the quadratic dependence of excitatory variability on input variability to the E- and P-populations, as well as its independence to input from the other two inhibitory populations.
source: EPI revealed the quadratic dependence of excitatory variability on input variability to the E- and P-populations, as well as its independence to input from the other two inhibitory populations.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the findings from the V1 analysis.

claim: The sensitive and degenerate parameters are intractable to predict mathematically, since the covariance matrix depends on the steady-state solution of the network.
source: Nevertheless, the sensitive and degenerate parameters are intractable to predict mathematically, since the covariance matrix depends on the steady-state solution of the network (Hennequin et al., 2018; Gardiner, 2009), and terms in the covariance expression increase quadratically with each additional neuron-type population (see also Section 'Primary visual cortex: Mathematical intuition and challenges').
evidence: This is a statement about the mathematical complexity of the V1 model, supported by citations and reference to a later section.

claim: By pointing out this mathematical complexity, we emphasize the value of EPI for gaining understanding about theoretical models when mathematical analysis becomes onerous or impractical.
source: By pointing out this mathematical complexity, we emphasize the value of EPI for gaining understanding about theoretical models when mathematical analysis becomes onerous or impractical.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of EPI.

claim: Rats can learn to switch from one behavioral task to the next on randomly interleaved trials.
source: It has been shown that rats can learn to switch from one behavioral task to the next on randomly interleaved trials (Duan et al., 2015), and an important question is what neural mechanisms produce this computation.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental findings, supported by a citation.

claim: Pharmacological inactivation of the SC impaired rat performance in the rapid task switching experiment.
source: Pharmacological inactivation of the SC impaired rat performance, and time-specific optogenetic inactivation revealed a crucial role for the SC on the cognitively demanding Anti trials (Duan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental findings, supported by a citation.

claim: Time-specific optogenetic inactivation revealed a crucial role for the SC on the cognitively demanding Anti trials.
source: Pharmacological inactivation of the SC impaired rat performance, and time-specific optogenetic inactivation revealed a crucial role for the SC on the cognitively demanding Anti trials (Duan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental findings, supported by a citation.

claim: These results motivated a nonlinear dynamical model of the SC containing four functionally defined neuron-type populations.
source: These results motivated a nonlinear dynamical model of the SC containing four functionally defined neuron-type populations.
evidence: This is a statement about the motivation for the SC model.

claim: In Duan et al., 2021, a computationally intensive procedure was used to obtain a set of 373 connectivity parameters that qualitatively reproduced these optogenetic inactivation results.
source: In Duan et al., 2021, a computationally intensive procedure was used to obtain a set of 373 connectivity parameters that qualitatively reproduced these optogenetic inactivation results.
evidence: This is a statement about prior work, supported by a citation.

claim: EPI is used to identify and characterize two linked, yet distinct regimes of rapid task switching connectivity.
source: To build upon the insights of this previous work, we use the probabilistic tools afforded by EPI to identify and characterize two linked, yet distinct regimes of rapid task switching connectivity.
evidence: This is a statement about the application of EPI to the SC model.

claim: The EPI inferred distribution produces Pro- and Anti-task accuracies consistent with rapid task switching.
source: The EPI inferred distribution (Figure 4C) produces Pro- and Anti-task accuracies (Figure 4C, bottom-left) consistent with rapid task switching (Equation 9).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of the SC analysis, supported by reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The EPI parameter distribution has rich structure that is not captured well by simple linear correlations.
source: This parameter distribution has rich structure that is not captured well by simple linear correlations (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of the SC analysis, supported by reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The shape of the EPI distribution is sharply bent, matching ground truth structure indicated by brute-force sampling.
source: Specifically, the shape of the EPI distribution is sharply bent, matching ground truth structure indicated by brute-force sampling (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of the SC analysis, supported by reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: These two directionalities of sensitivity motivate the distinction of connectivity into two regimes, which produce different types of responses in the Pro and Anti tasks.
source: These two directionalities of sensitivity motivate the distinction of connectivity into two regimes, which produce different types of responses in the Pro and Anti tasks (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).

claim: The sharp change in local structure of the EPI distribution is explained by distinct sensitivities: Anti-accuracy diminishes in only one or both directions of the sensitivity perturbation.
